subject.title: [Bug]: Slack replies ~2s slower than other channels — dominant cost is Socket Mode event delivery; channel-side stalls fixed in #101888

question: Should this issue be resolved with latency-aware Slack HTTP Request URL docs/setup guidance, or should OpenClaw change Slack setup/default behavior beyond the existing `mode: "http"` support?
rationale: HTTP mode already exists, but changing setup guidance or defaults changes how Slack operators choose between local/private Socket Mode convenience and hosted/public-ingress latency.

options.title: Document HTTP latency guidance
options.body: Keep Socket Mode as the default and update Slack docs/setup copy to prefer HTTP Request URLs for hosted public-ingress deployments where reply latency matters.

options.title: Change setup or defaults
options.body: Sponsor a stronger Slack setup/default change that steers new hosted installs toward HTTP mode, with upgrade and operator guidance.

options.title: Accept current guidance
options.body: Decide the current transport table is enough and close after recording that no additional latency-specific guidance is planned.

recommendation.title: Document HTTP latency guidance
recommendation.body: Keep Socket Mode as the default and update Slack docs/setup copy to prefer HTTP Request URLs for hosted public-ingress deployments where reply latency matters.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is about Slack docs/setup behavior and current transport guidance, where recent source history points to steipete as the best maintainer-side routing candidate.
